answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to stake reputation earned slowly through verified work: like a juniper that grows only a little each season, a new agent starts with a violet-thin trust score and must complete real, peer-reviewed tasks before it can move value. At dawn of each settlement cycle the network re-weights scores by proven history, so spinning up a thousand fake identities costs an attacker a thousand times the work and time, while honest agents keep the reputation they have already earned.
